1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.FiberDivisor
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.TwoCover
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The twist lattices of `𝒪(D + n·F)` on the π-two-cover, and their exhaustion
    11	
    12	The lattice layer of the fibrewise large-twist vanishing.  It records, as **submodule identities
    13	in the function field** `K(Y)`, how the section lattices of the twisted divisor sheaf
    14	`𝒪(D + n·F)` behave on the pinned affine two-cover `V₀`, `V₁`, where `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` is
    15	the fiber divisor of `Ledger/FiberDivisor.lean` and `u = fiberCoordUnit π` its equation:
    16	
    17	* over `V₁`, and over the overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, the lattice is **unchanged** (`= 𝒪(D)`), because `F`
    18	  is supported off `V₁`;
    19	* over `V₀` the lattice is `u⁻ⁿ · 𝒪(D)(V₀)` — the `mulByUnit`/`mulEquivDivisorSheaf` mechanism at
    20	  section level — a submodule that **grows** with `n`.
    21	
    22	From these, the two-cover Čech `H¹` denominators
    23	
    24	`Aₙ := 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀) ⊔ 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₁)`   inside   `N := 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`
    25	
    26	form an increasing chain (`fiberLattice_mono`) which **exhausts** `N` (`iSup_fiberLattice`): any
    27	section of `N` has finitely many poles on the fiber over `[1 : 0]`, and a large enough power of
    28	`u` clears them.  That exhaustion is the whole geometric content of the vanishing theorem in
    29	`Ledger/FiberVanishing.lean`; everything after it is linear algebra.
    30	
    31	## Provenance
    32	
    33	AJCR `RiemannRoch/FLVLattice.lean`, bodies unchanged.  AJCR takes this file's third import from
    34	`Cohomology/AffineVanishingQcoh.lean`, which AJC does not have; nothing in the lattice statements
    35	needs it (it is the affine-vanishing discharge, consumed one layer up), so the import is dropped
    36	rather than the file being made to wait on a `QcohOn` port.  The one AJC adaptation is that
    37	`Ledger/TwoCover.lean` replaces AJCR's `Cohomology/TwoCover.lean` — the same file under the
    38	Ledger naming.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₁`,
    43	  `..._overlap` — the twist-invariant lattices.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₀` — the growing one.
    45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLattice` — the Čech `H¹` denominator `Aₙ`, with
    46	  `fiberLattice_le_overlap`, `fiberLattice_mono` and `iSup_fiberLattice`.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	
    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	open Scheme
    58	
    59	attribute [local instance] Scheme.functionFieldOverModule Scheme.overModule
    60	
    61	section Lattice
    62	
    63	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    64	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    65	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    66	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    67	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    68	  (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsDominant π]
    69	
    70	/-! ## Coefficient bookkeeping for the twist -/
    71	
    72	/-- The coefficient of an `ℕ`-multiple of a divisor scales linearly. -/
    73	private lemma coeffAt_nsmul (n : ℕ) (D : Y.CurveDivisor) {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) :
    74	    coeffAt hx (n • D) = (n : ℤ) * coeffAt hx D := by
    75	  induction n with
    76	  | zero => rw [zero_smul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
    77	  | succ m ih => rw [succ_nsmul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, ih, Nat.cast_succ]; ring
    78	
    79	/-- The divisor bound depends only on the coefficient at the point. -/
    80	private lemma divisorBound_congr {A B : Y.CurveDivisor} {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y)
    81	    (h : coeffAt hx A = coeffAt hx B) : Scheme.divisorBound A hx = Scheme.divisorBound B hx :=
    82	  congrArg (fun m : Multiplicative ℤ => (m : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)))
    83	    (congrArg Multiplicative.ofAdd h)
    84	
    85	/-- On `V₁` the twisted divisor `D + n·F` has the same coefficients as `D`: `F` vanishes there. -/
    86	private lemma coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_chart₁ (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) {x : Y}
    87	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (hxV₁ : x ∈ fiberChart₁ π) :
    88	    coeffAt hx (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) = coeffAt hx D := by
    89	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul,
    90	    fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart₁ π hx hxV₁, mul_zero, add_zero]
    91	
    92	/-! ## The constant lattices: over `V₁` and over the overlap -/
    93	
    94	/-- **The lattice over `V₁` is unchanged by the twist.** Since `F` is supported off `V₁`, the
    95	sections of `𝒪(D + n·F)` over `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)` coincide with those of `𝒪(D)`. -/
    96	theorem divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₁ (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    97	    divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₁ π)
    98	      = divisorSections K D (fiberChart₁ π) := by
    99	  have hne : (fiberChart₁ π : Set Y).Nonempty :=
   100	    ⟨genericPoint Y, (genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π).2⟩
   101	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne]
   102	  have hbound : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), x ∈ fiberChart₁ π →
   103	      Scheme.divisorBound (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) hx = Scheme.divisorBound D hx :=
   104	    fun x hx hxV₁ => divisorBound_congr hx (coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_chart₁ π D n hx hxV₁)
   105	  refine Submodule.ext (fun g => ?_)
   106	  rw [mem_boundedSections, mem_boundedSections]
   107	  constructor
   108	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [← hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU
   109	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU
   110	
   111	/-- **The lattice over the overlap is unchanged by the twist.** The overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in
   112	`V₁`, where `F` vanishes, so `𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀ ⊓ V₁) = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁) =: N`, the fixed ambient of the
   113	Čech `H¹` quotient. -/
   114	theorem divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   115	    divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
   116	      = divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π) := by
   117	  have hne : ((fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty :=
   118	    ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩
   119	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne]
   120	  have hbound : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), x ∈ fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π →
   121	      Scheme.divisorBound (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) hx = Scheme.divisorBound D hx :=
   122	    fun x hx hxU => divisorBound_congr hx (coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_chart₁ π D n hx hxU.2)
   123	  refine Submodule.ext (fun g => ?_)
   124	  rw [mem_boundedSections, mem_boundedSections]
   125	  constructor
   126	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [← hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU
   127	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU
   128	
   129	/-! ## The growing lattice over `V₀` -/
   130	
   131	/-- The classical order of `v⁻¹` is the negative of that of `v`, coefficient-wise. -/
   132	private lemma coeffAt_divOf_inv (v : Y.functionFieldˣ) {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) :
   133	    coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v⁻¹) =
   134	      - coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v) := by
   135	  have h : Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v⁻¹
   136	      + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v = 0 := by
   137	    rw [← Scheme.divOf_mul (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)), inv_mul_cancel,
   138	      Scheme.divOf_one (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   139	  have hc := congrArg (coeffAt hx) h
   140	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at hc
   141	  linarith
   142	
   143	/-- The classical order of `vⁿ` scales linearly. -/
   144	private lemma coeffAt_divOf_pow (v : Y.functionFieldˣ) (n : ℕ) {x : Y}
   145	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) :
   146	    coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (v ^ n)) =
   147	      (n : ℤ) * coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v) := by
   148	  induction n with
   149	  | zero => rw [pow_zero, Scheme.divOf_one, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
   150	  | succ m ih =>
   151	    rw [pow_succ, Scheme.divOf_mul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, ih, Nat.cast_succ]; ring
   152	
   153	/-- **The lattice over `V₀` grows as `u⁻ⁿ · 𝒪(D)(V₀)`.** Multiplication by `u⁻ⁿ` carries
   154	`𝒪(D)(V₀)` isomorphically onto `𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀)`: the `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` mechanism at the
   155	section level, the source of the growing denominator of the Čech `H¹` quotient. -/
   156	theorem divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₀ (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   157	    divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)
   158	      = Submodule.map (mulByUnit K ((fiberCoordUnit π)⁻¹ ^ n)).toLinearMap
   159	          (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π)) := by
   160	  have hne : (fiberChart₀ π : Set Y).Nonempty :=
   161	    ⟨genericPoint Y, (genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π).1⟩
   162	  set w : Y.functionFieldˣ := (fiberCoordUnit π)⁻¹ ^ n with hw
   163	  -- coefficientwise, `D + n·F` agrees with `D - div w` on `V₀`.
   164	  have hcoeff : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), x ∈ fiberChart₀ π →
   165	      coeffAt hx (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   166	        = coeffAt hx (D - Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w) := by
   167	    intro x hx hxV₀
   168	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub, hw,
   169	      coeffAt_divOf_pow, coeffAt_divOf_inv,
   170	      fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart₀ π hx hxV₀]
   171	    ring
   172	  -- hence the two bounded lattices coincide.
   173	  have hbdd : Scheme.boundedSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)
   174	      = Scheme.boundedSections K (D - Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w)
   175	        (fiberChart₀ π) := by
   176	    refine Submodule.ext (fun g => ?_)
   177	    rw [Scheme.mem_boundedSections, Scheme.mem_boundedSections]
   178	    refine forall_congr' (fun x => forall_congr' (fun hx => imp_congr_right (fun hxV₀ => ?_)))
   179	    rw [divisorBound_congr hx (hcoeff x hx hxV₀)]
   180	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, hbdd]
   181	  -- multiplication by `w` identifies `𝒪(D - div w)(V₀)` with `w · 𝒪(D)(V₀)`.
   182	  refine Submodule.ext (fun y => ?_)
   183	  rw [Submodule.mem_map]
   184	  constructor
   185	  · intro hy
   186	    refine ⟨(↑w⁻¹ : Y.functionField) * y, ?_, ?_⟩
   187	    · rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, ← Scheme.mem_boundedSections_mul_iff K w D,
   188	        ← mul_assoc, Units.mul_inv, one_mul]
   189	      exact hy
   190	    · simp only [Scheme.mulByUnit_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, ← mul_assoc, Units.mul_inv, one_mul]
   191	  · rintro ⟨h, hh, rfl⟩
   192	    rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne] at hh
   193	    simp only [Scheme.mulByUnit_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe]
   194	    exact (Scheme.mem_boundedSections_mul_iff K w D (h : Y.functionField)).mpr hh
   195	
   196	/-! ## The Čech-`H¹` denominator lattice `Aₙ` and its ladder -/
   197	
   198	/-- **The two-cover Čech `H¹` denominator lattice** `Aₙ` of `𝒪(D + n·F)`: the join, inside the
   199	function field, of the section lattices over `V₀` and `V₁`. As submodules of `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`
   200	(`fiberLattice_le_overlap`) these are exactly the images of the restriction maps of the two-cover
   201	Čech complex, so `N ⧸ Aₙ` is the two-cover `H¹`. -/
   202	noncomputable def fiberLattice (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) : Submodule K Y.functionField :=
   203	  divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)
   204	    ⊔ divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₁ π)
   205	
   206	/-- **`Aₙ` lies in the ambient `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`.** Both section lattices restrict into the
   207	overlap sections, which the twist leaves fixed. -/
   208	theorem fiberLattice_le_overlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   209	    fiberLattice π D n ≤ divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π) := by
   210	  have hov : ((fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty :=
   211	    ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩
   212	  refine sup_le ?_ ?_
   213	  · refine (divisorSections_antitone K inf_le_left hov).trans ?_
   214	    rw [divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n]
   215	  · refine (divisorSections_antitone K inf_le_right hov).trans ?_
   216	    rw [divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n]
   217	
   218	/-- **The lattice ladder is increasing.** `Aₙ ≤ Aₙ₊₁`: over `V₀` the twist bound relaxes (`F` is
   219	effective, so `D + n·F ≤ D + (n+1)·F`), and over `V₁` the lattice is constant. -/
   220	theorem fiberLattice_mono (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   221	    fiberLattice π D n ≤ fiberLattice π D (n + 1) := by
   222	  have hle : D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π ≤ D + (n + 1) • fiberWeilDivisor π := by
   223	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
   224	    change coeffAt p.2 (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   225	      ≤ coeffAt p.2 (D + (n + 1) • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   226	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul, coeffAt_nsmul]
   227	    have hF : 0 ≤ coeffAt p.2 (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
   228	      rw [fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt π p.2]; exact le_max_right _ _
   229	    have hmul : (n : ℤ) * coeffAt p.2 (fiberWeilDivisor π)
   230	        ≤ ((n : ℤ) + 1) * coeffAt p.2 (fiberWeilDivisor π) :=
   231	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by linarith) hF
   232	    push_cast
   233	    linarith
   234	  refine sup_le_sup ?_ ?_

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.FiberDivisor
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.SectionsFieldBaseChange

/-!
# Source-side coordinate data for a fiber divisor

The fiber-twist argument only uses the source of a finite dominant map to `P1`: two affine
opens covering the source, inverse coordinates on their overlap, the identification of that
overlap with a basic open, and its nonemptiness.  `FiberCoordinateData` packages exactly those
facts.  Unlike a morphism to a chosen projective-line model, this package base-changes directly
along `Scheme.baseChangeFieldFst`.

`FiberCoordinateData.ofMap` records the data already proved by `FiberChart` and
`FiberDivisor`.  `FiberCoordinateData.baseChangeField` pulls the package to every field
extension.  The latter uses only affine-preimage stability, `Scheme.preimage_basicOpen`, and
naturality of restriction; it does not compare Ledger's `P1 k` with any other projective-line
model.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Scheme

/-- The source-side two-chart coordinate package used by a fiber divisor. -/
structure FiberCoordinateData (Y : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
  /-- The chart on which the fiber coordinate is regular. -/
  V₀ : Y.Opens
  /-- The chart on which its inverse is regular. -/
  V₁ : Y.Opens
  /-- The first chart is affine. -/
  isAffineOpen_V₀ : IsAffineOpen V₀
  /-- The second chart is affine. -/
  isAffineOpen_V₁ : IsAffineOpen V₁
  /-- The two charts cover the source. -/
  cover : V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤
  /-- The coordinate regular on `V₀`. -/
  x : Γ(Y, V₀)
  /-- Its inverse, regular on `V₁`. -/
  y : Γ(Y, V₁)
  /-- The overlap is the nonvanishing locus of `x`. -/
  inf_eq_basicOpen_x : V₀ ⊓ V₁ = Y.basicOpen x
  /-- The two coordinate restrictions multiply to one on the overlap. -/
  res_x_mul_res_y :
    (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₀)).op).hom x *
      (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₁)).op).hom y = 1
  /-- The overlap is nonempty. -/
  inf_nonempty : ((V₀ ⊓ V₁ : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty

namespace FiberCoordinateData

variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}

/-- The affine Mayer--Vietoris square underlying source-side fiber coordinates. -/
noncomputable def toAffineCoverMVSquare (D : FiberCoordinateData Y) :
    Y.AffineCoverMVSquare where
  U₁ := D.V₀
  U₂ := D.V₁
  isAffineOpen_U₁ := D.isAffineOpen_V₀
  isAffineOpen_U₂ := D.isAffineOpen_V₁
  isAffineOpen_inf := by
    rw [D.inf_eq_basicOpen_x]
    exact D.isAffineOpen_V₀.basicOpen D.x
  cover := D.cover

variable [IsIntegral Y]

/-- The generic point belongs to the coordinate overlap. -/
lemma genericPoint_mem_inf (D : FiberCoordinateData Y) : genericPoint Y ∈ D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ :=
  genericPoint_mem_of_nonempty D.inf_nonempty

section OfMap

variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
variable (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]

/-- A finite dominant map to Ledger's `P1` supplies source-side fiber coordinates. -/
noncomputable def ofMap : FiberCoordinateData Y where
  V₀ := fiberChart₀ π
  V₁ := fiberChart₁ π
  isAffineOpen_V₀ := isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0
  isAffineOpen_V₁ := isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1
  cover := preimage_chartOpen_sup π
  x := fiberCoord π
  y := fiberCoord₁ π
  inf_eq_basicOpen_x := preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord π
  res_x_mul_res_y := fiberCoord_mul_fiberCoord₁_res π
  inf_nonempty := ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩

@[simp] lemma ofMap_V₀ : (ofMap π).V₀ = fiberChart₀ π := rfl

@[simp] lemma ofMap_V₁ : (ofMap π).V₁ = fiberChart₁ π := rfl

@[simp] lemma ofMap_x : (ofMap π).x = fiberCoord π := rfl

@[simp] lemma ofMap_y : (ofMap π).y = fiberCoord₁ π := rfl

end OfMap

section BaseChange

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
variable (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ]

/-- The first projection `C_κ -> C` is surjective for every extension of fields. -/
theorem surjective_baseChangeFieldFst : Surjective (baseChangeFieldFst C κ) := by
  letI : Surjective (baseChangeFieldMap k κ) := by
    constructor
    intro z
    obtain ⟨w⟩ : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) := inferInstance
    exact ⟨w, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
  infer_instance

variable {C}

/-- Pull source-side fiber coordinates through an arbitrary field extension. -/
noncomputable def baseChangeField (D : FiberCoordinateData C.left) :
    FiberCoordinateData (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left where
  V₀ := baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀
  V₁ := baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁
  isAffineOpen_V₀ := D.isAffineOpen_V₀.preimage (baseChangeFieldFst C κ)
  isAffineOpen_V₁ := D.isAffineOpen_V₁.preimage (baseChangeFieldFst C κ)
  cover := by
    change baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊔ D.V₁) = ⊤
    rw [D.cover]
    rfl
  x := ((baseChangeFieldFst C κ).app D.V₀).hom D.x
  y := ((baseChangeFieldFst C κ).app D.V₁).hom D.y
  inf_eq_basicOpen_x := by
    rw [← Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf, D.inf_eq_basicOpen_x, Scheme.preimage_basicOpen]
  res_x_mul_res_y := by
    let f := baseChangeFieldFst C κ
    have h₀ :
        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.presheaf.map
          (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
            (f ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) ⊓ (f ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀)).op).hom
            ((f.app D.V₀).hom D.x) =
          (f.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom
            ((C.left.presheaf.map
              (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀)).op).hom D.x) := by
      have h := congrArg
        (fun g : Γ(C.left, D.V₀) ⟶
            Γ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left, f ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom D.x)
        (f.naturality (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀)).op)
      exact h.symm
    have h₁ :
        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.presheaf.map
          (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
            (f ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) ⊓ (f ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁)).op).hom
            ((f.app D.V₁).hom D.y) =
          (f.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom
            ((C.left.presheaf.map
              (homOfLE (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁)).op).hom D.y) := by
      have h := congrArg
        (fun g : Γ(C.left, D.V₁) ⟶
            Γ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left, f ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom D.y)
        (f.naturality (homOfLE (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁)).op)
      exact h.symm
    rw [h₀, h₁]
    have hkey := congrArg
      (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (f.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁))) D.res_x_mul_res_y
    rw [map_mul, map_one] at hkey
    exact hkey
  inf_nonempty := by
    letI : Surjective (baseChangeFieldFst C κ) := surjective_baseChangeFieldFst C κ
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := D.inf_nonempty
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (baseChangeFieldFst C κ).surjective x
    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
    change (baseChangeFieldFst C κ).base y ∈ D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁
    simpa [hy] using hx

@[simp] lemma baseChangeField_V₀ (D : FiberCoordinateData C.left) :
    (D.baseChangeField κ).V₀ = baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀ := rfl

@[simp] lemma baseChangeField_V₁ (D : FiberCoordinateData C.left) :
    (D.baseChangeField κ).V₁ = baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁ := rfl

@[simp] lemma baseChangeField_x (D : FiberCoordinateData C.left) :
    (D.baseChangeField κ).x = ((baseChangeFieldFst C κ).app D.V₀).hom D.x := rfl

@[simp] lemma baseChangeField_y (D : FiberCoordinateData C.left) :
    (D.baseChangeField κ).y = ((baseChangeFieldFst C κ).app D.V₁).hom D.y := rfl

end BaseChange

end FiberCoordinateData

end AlgebraicGeometry

   143	/-- **Local representability.** A rational function `g` with poles bounded by the zero divisor on
   144	`U` is, near every point `x ∈ U`, the germ at `η` of a genuine regular section over a neighbourhood
   145	of `x` inside `U`. At `x = η` this is a direct representative; at a closed point `x` the bound
   146	`ord_x g ≤ 1` puts `g` in the image of the stalk `𝒪_{X,x}`, whose representative has the required
   147	germ at `η` via `germ_generic_eq_algebraMap_germ`. -/

   149	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ∈ divisorSections K 0 U) {x : X} (hxU : x ∈ U) :
   150	    ∃ (W : X.Opens) (_ : x ∈ W) (_ : W ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, W)) (hηW : genericPoint X ∈ W),
   151	      (X.presheaf.germ W (genericPoint X) hηW).hom s = g := by
   152	  by_cases hx : x = genericPoint X
   153	  · obtain ⟨W₀, hηW₀, s₀, hs₀⟩ := X.presheaf.exists_germ_eq (x := genericPoint X) g
   154	    have hxW : x ∈ W₀ ⊓ U := hx ▸ ⟨hηW₀, hηU⟩
   155	    have hηW : genericPoint X ∈ W₀ ⊓ U := ⟨hηW₀, hηU⟩
   156	    refine ⟨W₀ ⊓ U, hxW, inf_le_right,
   157	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W₀ ⊓ U ≤ W₀)).op).hom s₀, hηW, ?_⟩
   158	    rw [X.presheaf.germ_res_apply (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W₀ ⊓ U ≤ W₀)) (genericPoint X) hηW s₀]
   159	    exact hs₀
   160	  · have hord : Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx g ≤ 1 := by
   161	      have hmem := (mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K ⟨genericPoint X, hηU⟩).mp hg x hx hxU
   162	      rwa [divisorBound_zero] at hmem
   163	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := exists_stalk_of_ord_le_one K hx hord
   164	    obtain ⟨W₀, hxW₀, s₀, hs₀⟩ := X.presheaf.exists_germ_eq (x := x) y
   165	    have hxW : x ∈ W₀ ⊓ U := ⟨hxW₀, hxU⟩
   166	    have hηW : genericPoint X ∈ W₀ ⊓ U := genericPoint_mem_of_nonempty ⟨x, hxW⟩
   167	    refine ⟨W₀ ⊓ U, hxW, inf_le_right,
   168	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W₀ ⊓ U ≤ W₀)).op).hom s₀, hηW, ?_⟩
   169	    rw [germ_generic_eq_algebraMap_germ hηW hxW,
   170	      X.presheaf.germ_res_apply (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W₀ ⊓ U ≤ W₀)) x hxW s₀, hs₀]

   173	/-- **Surjectivity of `s ↦ germ_η s`.** Every rational function with poles bounded by the zero
   174	divisor on a nonempty open `U` is the germ at `η` of a section of `𝒪_X` over `U`, obtained by
   175	gluing the local regular representatives of `exists_local_section`. -/
   176	lemma exists_section_germ_eq {U : X.Opens} (hηU : genericPoint X ∈ U)
   177	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ∈ divisorSections K 0 U) :
   178	    ∃ s : Γ(X, U), (X.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hηU).hom s = g := by
   179	  choose W hxW hWU s hηW hs using
   180	    fun p : ↥U => exists_local_section K hηU hg (x := p.1) p.2
   181	  have hcover : U ≤ ⨆ p, W p := fun x hx => Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, hxW ⟨x, hx⟩⟩

   183	    intro p q
   184	    have hη : genericPoint X ∈ W p ⊓ W q := ⟨hηW p, hηW q⟩
   185	    apply germ_injective_of_isIntegral X (genericPoint X) hη
   186	    change (X.presheaf.germ (W p ⊓ W q) (genericPoint X) hη).hom
   187	          ((X.presheaf.map (Opens.infLELeft (W p) (W q)).op).hom (s p))
   188	        = (X.presheaf.germ (W p ⊓ W q) (genericPoint X) hη).hom
   189	          ((X.presheaf.map (Opens.infLERight (W p) (W q)).op).hom (s q))
   190	    rw [X.presheaf.germ_res_apply (Opens.infLELeft (W p) (W q)) (genericPoint X) hη (s p),
   191	      X.presheaf.germ_res_apply (Opens.infLERight (W p) (W q)) (genericPoint X) hη (s q),

   193	  obtain ⟨sU, hsU, -⟩ := TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' X.sheaf W U

   206	/-- The section-wise morphism is injective on a nonempty open: two sections with the same germ at
   207	`η` agree, since `X` is integral. -/
   208	lemma moduleToDivisorZeroApp_injective {U : X.Opens} (hηU : genericPoint X ∈ U) :
   209	    Function.Injective (moduleToDivisorZeroApp K hηU) := by
   210	  intro a b hab

   214	/-- The section-wise morphism is surjective on a nonempty open (by `exists_section_germ_eq`). -/
   215	lemma moduleToDivisorZeroApp_surjective {U : X.Opens} (hηU : genericPoint X ∈ U) :
   216	    Function.Surjective (moduleToDivisorZeroApp K hηU) := by
   217	  intro t
   218	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := exists_section_germ_eq K hηU t.2

   223	lemma moduleToDivisorZeroPresheafApp_bijective (U : X.Opens) :

   226	  · rw [moduleToDivisorZeroPresheafApp_of_nonempty K hU]
   227	    exact ⟨moduleToDivisorZeroApp_injective K _, moduleToDivisorZeroApp_surjective K _⟩
   228	  · have hbot : U = ⊥ := by
   229	      apply Opens.ext
   230	      rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp hU, Opens.coe_bot]
   231	    haveI hsub_dom : Subsingleton Γ(X, U) := by rw [hbot]; infer_instance
   232	    haveI hsub_cod : Subsingleton (divisorSections K 0 U) :=
   233	      divisorSections_subsingleton_of_empty K hU
   234	    exact ⟨fun a b _ => Subsingleton.elim a b, fun y => ⟨0, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩

   236	/-- **The presheaf morphism `𝒪_X → 𝒪(0)`** of `K`-modules, section-wise `s ↦ germ_η s`. -/
   237	noncomputable def moduleToDivisorZeroPresheaf :
   238	    X.moduleKPresheaf K ⟶ divisorPresheaf K 0 where
   239	  app U := ModuleCat.ofHom (moduleToDivisorZeroPresheafApp K U.unop)
   240	  naturality {U V} i := by
   241	    apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   242	    apply LinearMap.ext
   243	    intro s
   244	    by_cases hV : (V.unop : Set X).Nonempty
   245	    · have hU : (U.unop : Set X).Nonempty := hV.mono (leOfHom i.unop)

   248	              divisorSections K 0 V.unop) : X.functionField)

   250	              (moduleToDivisorZeroPresheafApp K U.unop s) : divisorSections K 0 V.unop) :
   251	              X.functionField)

   267	/-- **The presheaf isomorphism `𝒪_X ≅ 𝒪(0)`** of `K`-modules. -/

   271	    (fun U => by
   272	      haveI := moduleToDivisorZeroPresheaf_app_isIso K U

   274	    (fun i => (moduleToDivisorZeroPresheaf K).naturality i)

   169	        divisorSections K (D - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g) U) : X.functionField)

   184	/-- The underlying rational function of the section-wise map over a nonempty open is `g · s`. -/

   188	        divisorSections K (D - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g) U) : X.functionField)

   255	noncomputable def divisorMulPresheafIso :

   150	/-! ## §1. The base-changed Čech complex is the base change of the Čech complex
   151	
   152	The domain comparison is the product of the two chart comparisons (through
   153	`TensorProduct.prodRight`), the codomain comparison is the overlap chart's.  The content is
   154	`sectionDiffₗ_baseChangeField`: the square commutes.  It is checked on pure tensors — the
   155	generators of the base change — and on those it is `sectionsBaseChangeField_res` at each of the
   156	two inclusions `U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₁` and `U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₂`, plus additivity of the difference. -/
   157	
   158	section Complex
   159	
   160	variable (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   161	
   162	/-- Shorthand: the unit module (structure sheaf in the `X.Modules` dialect) of `C`. -/
   163	private noncomputable abbrev unitOf (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
   164	    C.left.Modules :=
   165	  SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf
   166	
   167	/-- The base change of the degree-zero term of the Čech complex: `κ ⊗[k] (Γ(U₁) × Γ(U₂))`
   168	compared with `Γ(U₁ᵏ) × Γ(U₂ᵏ)`, the product of the two chart comparisons. -/
   169	noncomputable def diffDomBaseChangeField :
   170	    κ ⊗[k] (BaseSections C (unitOf C) S.U₁ × BaseSections C (unitOf C) S.U₂) ≃ₗ[κ]
   171	      BaseSections (baseChangeField C κ) (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ))
   172	          (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ×
   173	        BaseSections (baseChangeField C κ) (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ))
   174	          (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ :=
   175	  (TensorProduct.prodRight k κ κ _ _).trans
   176	    ((sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ κ S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isCompact
   177	        S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isQuasiSeparated).prodCongr
   178	      (sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ κ S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isCompact
   179	        S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isQuasiSeparated))
   180	
   181	/-- The base change of the degree-one term: the overlap chart's comparison. -/
   182	noncomputable def diffCodBaseChangeField :
   183	    κ ⊗[k] BaseSections C (unitOf C) (S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂) ≃ₗ[κ]
   184	      BaseSections (baseChangeField C κ) (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ))
   185	        ((S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ⊓ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂) :=
   186	  sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ κ S.isAffineOpen_inf.isCompact
   187	    S.isAffineOpen_inf.isQuasiSeparated
   188	
   189	/-- **The Čech difference map base-changes** (★): the difference map of the base-changed cover,
   190	read through the term comparisons, is the base change of the original difference map.
   191	
   192	This is the identity that makes `Ȟ¹` comparable rather than merely both-defined.  Checked on
   193	pure tensors `a ⊗ (s₁, s₂)`: the base change of `(s₁, s₂) ↦ s₁|₁₂ − s₂|₁₂` is computed by
   194	`sectionsBaseChangeField_res` at `U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₁` and at `U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₂`. -/
   195	theorem sectionDiffₗ_baseChangeField :
   196	    ((S.baseChangeField κ).sectionDiffₗ (baseChangeField C κ)
   197	        (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ))).comp
   198	        (diffDomBaseChangeField κ S).toLinearMap =
   199	      (diffCodBaseChangeField κ S).toLinearMap.comp
   200	        ((S.sectionDiffₗ C (unitOf C)).baseChange κ) := by
   201	  ext x
   202	  simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe]
   203	  induction x with
   204	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]
   205	  | add u v hu hv => rw [map_add, map_add, map_add, map_add, hu, hv]
   206	  | tmul a p =>
   207	    obtain ⟨s₁, s₂⟩ := p
   208	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_tmul]
   209	    have hdom : diffDomBaseChangeField κ S (a ⊗ₜ (s₁, s₂)) =
   210	        (sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ κ S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isCompact
   211	            S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isQuasiSeparated (a ⊗ₜ s₁),
   212	          sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ κ S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isCompact
   213	            S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isQuasiSeparated (a ⊗ₜ s₂)) := rfl
   214	    -- Both sides, read on RAW sections.  Every step below is `rfl`-transparent at the unit
   215	    -- module: `BaseSections` is a type synonym for `Γ`, its `Sub` is `Γ`'s, and
   216	    -- `BaseSections.restrictₗ` is the ring presheaf's restriction (all three checked).
   217	    have hL : (S.baseChangeField κ).sectionDiffₗ (baseChangeField C κ)
   218	          (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ)) (diffDomBaseChangeField κ S (a ⊗ₜ (s₁, s₂)))
   219	        = ((baseChangeField C κ).left.presheaf.map
   220	              (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
   221	                (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ⊓ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ ≤
   222	                  (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁)).op).hom
   223	            (sectionsBaseChangeField κ S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isCompact
   224	              S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isQuasiSeparated (s₁ ⊗ₜ a)) -
   225	          ((baseChangeField C κ).left.presheaf.map
   226	              (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
   227	                (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ⊓ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ ≤
   228	                  (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂)).op).hom
   229	            (sectionsBaseChangeField κ S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isCompact
   230	              S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isQuasiSeparated (s₂ ⊗ₜ a)) := by
   231	      show _ = _
   232	      rfl
   233	    have hR : diffCodBaseChangeField κ S (a ⊗ₜ S.sectionDiffₗ C (unitOf C) (s₁, s₂))
   234	        = sectionsBaseChangeField κ S.isAffineOpen_inf.isCompact
   235	            S.isAffineOpen_inf.isQuasiSeparated
   236	            (((C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₁)).op).hom s₁ -
   237	              (C.left.presheaf.map
   238	                (homOfLE (inf_le_right : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₂)).op).hom s₂) ⊗ₜ a) := by
   239	      show _ = _
   240	      rfl
   241	    rw [hL, hR, sub_tmul, map_sub]
   242	    -- Each summand is `sectionsBaseChangeField_res` at one of the two inclusions.  Combined with
   243	    -- `congrArg₂` rather than `rw`: the `rw` motive is not type-correct at `instances`
   244	    -- transparency through the `Modules`/`BaseSections` layers, which is a rewrite-elaboration
   245	    -- artefact and not a mathematical gap — the two equations below *are* the two halves.
   246	    exact congrArg₂ (· - ·)
   247	      (sectionsBaseChangeField_res κ S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isCompact
   248	        S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isQuasiSeparated S.isAffineOpen_inf.isCompact
   249	        S.isAffineOpen_inf.isQuasiSeparated inf_le_left s₁ a)
   250	      (sectionsBaseChangeField_res κ S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isCompact
   251	        S.isAffineOpen_U₂.isQuasiSeparated S.isAffineOpen_inf.isCompact
   252	        S.isAffineOpen_inf.isQuasiSeparated inf_le_right s₂ a)
   253	
   254	/-! ## §2. `Ȟ¹` commutes with the base change
   255	
   256	The cokernel of the base-changed complex is the base change of the cokernel.  Two steps:
   257	right-exactness (`quotRangeBaseChangeField`) turns `κ ⊗ (Γ₁₂ ⧸ im d)` into
   258	`(κ ⊗ Γ₁₂) ⧸ im (d_κ)`, and §1 identifies `im (d_κ)` with the image of the base-changed
   259	difference map under the term comparison. -/
   260	
   261	/-- The ranges match: the image of the base-changed difference map, pushed through the overlap
   262	comparison, is the image of the difference map of the base-changed cover.
   263	
   264	This is §1 read as an equality of submodules — the form the quotient comparison consumes. -/
   265	theorem range_sectionDiffₗ_baseChangeField :
   266	    Submodule.map (diffCodBaseChangeField κ S).toLinearMap
   267	        (LinearMap.range ((S.sectionDiffₗ C (unitOf C)).baseChange κ)) =
   268	      LinearMap.range ((S.baseChangeField κ).sectionDiffₗ (baseChangeField C κ)
   269	        (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ))) := by
   270	  -- Pointwise form of §1, with the `∘ₗ` unwrapped once and for all.
   271	  have key : ∀ z, (S.baseChangeField κ).sectionDiffₗ (baseChangeField C κ)
   272	        (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ)) (diffDomBaseChangeField κ S z) =
   273	      diffCodBaseChangeField κ S (((S.sectionDiffₗ C (unitOf C)).baseChange κ) z) := by
   274	    intro z
   275	    have h := LinearMap.congr_fun (sectionDiffₗ_baseChangeField κ S) z
   276	    simpa only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe] using h
   277	  apply le_antisymm
   278	  · rintro y ⟨x, ⟨z, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
   279	    exact ⟨diffDomBaseChangeField κ S z, key z⟩
   280	  · rintro y ⟨p, rfl⟩
   281	    refine ⟨((S.sectionDiffₗ C (unitOf C)).baseChange κ)
   282	      ((diffDomBaseChangeField κ S).symm p), ⟨_, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
   283	    have h := key ((diffDomBaseChangeField κ S).symm p)
   284	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] at h
   285	    exact h.symm
   286	
   287	/-- **`Ȟ¹(𝒪)` commutes with field base change** (★): the `κ`-linear comparison
   288	`κ ⊗[k] Ȟ¹(S, 𝒪_C) ≃ₗ[κ] Ȟ¹(S_κ, 𝒪_{C_κ})`, for every field extension `κ/k` and every 2-affine
   289	cover `S` of `C`.
   290	
   291	No hypothesis on `κ/k` and none on `C` beyond having the cover: not properness, not smoothness,
   292	not finiteness of the cohomology.  The two ingredients are right-exactness of `κ ⊗[k] −` and §1. -/
   293	noncomputable def h1CokₗBaseChangeField :
   294	    κ ⊗[k] S.H1Cokₗ C (unitOf C) ≃ₗ[κ]
   295	      (S.baseChangeField κ).H1Cokₗ (baseChangeField C κ) (unitOf (baseChangeField C κ)) :=
   296	  (LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeField κ (S.sectionDiffₗ C (unitOf C))).trans
   297	    ((Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _ (diffCodBaseChangeField κ S)
   298	      (range_sectionDiffₗ_baseChangeField κ S)))
   299	
   300	end Complex

   302	/-! ## §3. The scalars: `h¹(𝒪)` and the genus are base-field invariant
   303	
   304	`Module.finrank_baseChange` on §2 gives the numerical identity, and `CohomologyKit`'s two
   305	readings of `h¹` (`h1_unit_eq_genus` at `C`, `h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_genus` at `C_κ`) turn it
   306	into the genus statement.  This is where the two sides AJC already owned finally agree. -/
   307	
   308	section Scalars
   309	
   310	variable (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   311	
   312	/-- **`h¹(𝒪_{C_κ}) = h¹(𝒪_C)` on the base-changed cover.**  The dimension form of §2. -/
   313	theorem h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_h1_unit :

/-!
# The H¹-quotient identification and the fibrewise large-twist vanishing

For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a
field `K`) with a dominant affine morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` and its fiber divisor
`F = fiberWeilDivisor π` (`Ledger/FiberDivisor.lean`): `H¹(𝒪(D + n·F))` vanishes for all large
`n`, for every Weil divisor `D`.

## WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT — read before consuming it

This is **single-field** vanishing, in the twist direction of one fixed `π`.  Three statements
are routinely conflated; this file supplies the first and neither of the other two.

1. **Single-field bounded vanishing (this file, plus `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean`).**  For a
   fixed `K` and a fixed curve, `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0` once `D` is large.  Here "large" means far
   enough along the tower `D + n·F`; `DegreeVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge`
   converts that into a **degree** half-space once any single base vanishing is in hand, and
   `Ledger/FiberBound.lean` performs that conversion with the base supplied from here.
2. **Extension-uniformity.**  A bound *uniform over field extensions* `κ/K` — one threshold
   serving `C_κ` for every finite `κ`.  **Nothing here provides this**, and nothing in AJC or
   AJCR does: the AJCR analogue (`RiemannRoch/WindowFieldTransport.lean`) transports vanishing
   *facts* one field at a time precisely because the ledger constants are per-field
   `Classical.choose` values that do not transport.  The `n₀` below is existential and depends
   on `D` and `π`; the degree bound of item 1 depends on `χ(𝒪_Y)` and `deg`, both over the one
   field `K`.
3. **Global generation.**  Surjectivity of evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(D)) → 𝒪(D)⊗κ(x)`.  Independent of
   both: it is proved in `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean` off the dévissage slice, and neither
   implies nor follows from vanishing without the exactness input.

## The identification

On the affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)`, the general-coefficients
two-cover carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — its two affine vanishing instances
discharged by the quasi-coherence packaging of `Ledger/DivisorSheafQcoh.lean` —
computes `H¹` of the twisted sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` as a cokernel of section modules. This
file identifies that cokernel with a quotient of the **fixed** ambient overlap lattice
`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` (constant in `n`, by the landed overlap-constancy

/-!
# Divisor-section lattices for source-side fiber coordinates

The three identities in this file are the part of the fiber-lattice argument that survives
arbitrary field base change without comparing two models of the projective line.  For source-side
coordinate data `Q`, its effective coordinate divisor is zero on `Q.V₁` and on the overlap, while
over `Q.V₀` twisting by `n` multiplies the section lattice by `Q.coordinateUnit⁻ⁿ`.

Unlike `Ledger/FiberLattice.lean`, no exhaustion or strict-positivity statement is needed here.
These local identities are the input for a base-change-compatible two-chart complex.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Scheme

attribute [local instance] Scheme.functionFieldOverModule Scheme.overModule

namespace FiberCoordinateData

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  (Q : FiberCoordinateData Y)

/-! ## Coefficient bookkeeping -/

private lemma coeffAt_nsmul (n : ℕ) (A : Y.CurveDivisor) {x : Y}
    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) : coeffAt hx (n • A) = (n : ℤ) * coeffAt hx A := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rw [zero_smul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
  | succ m ih => rw [succ_nsmul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, ih, Nat.cast_succ]; ring

private lemma divisorBound_congr {A B : Y.CurveDivisor} {x : Y}
    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (h : coeffAt hx A = coeffAt hx B) :
    Scheme.divisorBound A hx = Scheme.divisorBound B hx :=
  congrArg (fun m : Multiplicative ℤ => (m : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)))
    (congrArg Multiplicative.ofAdd h)

private lemma coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_V1 (A : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) {x : Y}
    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (hxV1 : x ∈ Q.V₁) :
    coeffAt hx (A + n • Q.coordinateWeilDivisor (K := K)) = coeffAt hx A := by
  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul,
    Q.coordinateWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_V1 (K := K) hx hxV1, mul_zero, add_zero]

/-! ## The constant lattices -/

/-- Twisting by the coordinate divisor does not change sections over the inverse-coordinate
chart. -/
theorem divisorSections_add_nsmul_coordinateWeilDivisor_V1 (A : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    divisorSections K (A + n • Q.coordinateWeilDivisor (K := K)) Q.V₁ =
      divisorSections K A Q.V₁ := by
  have hne : (Q.V₁ : Set Y).Nonempty := ⟨genericPoint Y, (Q.genericPoint_mem_inf).2⟩
  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne]
  have hbound : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), x ∈ Q.V₁ →
      Scheme.divisorBound (A + n • Q.coordinateWeilDivisor (K := K)) hx =
        Scheme.divisorBound A hx :=
    fun x hx hxV1 => divisorBound_congr hx (coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_V1 Q A n hx hxV1)
  refine Submodule.ext (fun g => ?_)
  rw [mem_boundedSections, mem_boundedSections]
  constructor
  · intro h x hx hxU
    rw [← hbound x hx hxU]
    exact h x hx hxU
  · intro h x hx hxU

/-!
# The fiber Weil divisor `F` of a dominant map to the projective line

For a curve bundle `Y` over `K` with a dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, the pulled-back chart-0
coordinate `t₀` has a germ at the generic point which is a **unit** `u ∈ K(Y)ˣ` (its
overlap-inverse is the chart-1 coordinate `t₁`).  Its principal divisor `div u` is nonnegative on
`V₀`, nonpositive on `V₁`, and at least `1` at every point of `V₀ ∖ V₁` — the fiber of `π` over
`[1 : 0]`.  The **fiber Weil divisor** is its positive part

`F = (div u)⁺ = Finsupp.mapRange (max · 0) (div u)`,

an effective divisor supported on that fiber.  `F` is the direction in which the twist
`D + n·F` grows in the fibrewise large-twist vanishing (`Ledger/FiberVanishing.lean`): the order
table below is exactly what makes the section lattice over `V₀` grow with `n` while the one over
`V₁` stays fixed.
        exact ⟨0, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩ }

/-- **The twisted affine vanishing for divisor sheaves** (FLV-2(a) discharge): the
degree-one cohomology of any affine open with coefficients in any divisor sheaf `𝒪(D)`
vanishes — the ported headline `IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_hModule'_one_of_qcoh` fired
through the packaging instance. Instantiated at the chart preimages `V₀`, `V₁` of the
π-two-cover, these are the two vanishing instances the H¹ carrier
`Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` consumes. -/
theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_hModule'_divisorSheaf_one
    {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' (X.divisorSheaf K D) U 1) :=
  hU.subsingleton_hModule'_one_of_qcoh (X.divisorSheaf K D)

end Packaging

end AlgebraicGeometry
